source_text: So, what could be interesting would be to look at a small "flow" of turns, say 3 operator turns and 3 agent turns.  E.g. on line 23519 I had an idea, we could look at how operator intent to explore an idea relates to agent-follow-up over the next few turns, whether the design patterns that Kimi mined predicted anything from those exchanges, etc.

reply_text:
I've pulled the three operator turns and three replies starting at line 23519. Next I'm finding where Kimi's mined patterns for those turns are recorded.I've found how 象 read those three turns. Now checking one turn the graph puts between them, then writing up.㊥ (the flow from line 23519) I've read your three turns, my three replies, and how 象 read your turns. The aim in your idea held through the flow, but its source changed:
- **Your idea** was to learn the War Machine's R-node language from its agents' transcripts.
- **My reply** found that only 4 of 23 nodes have an agent talking.
- **You redirected** to codex-10's narrated step-through of a click.
- **You then said** to look where the narrative and the tree disagree, and my reply produced the six-node table.

The mined patterns predicted almost nothing here. 象 accepted only one pattern across the three turns, on the third. For the redirect, it read three candidates and rejected all three, so the library seems to have no pattern for "the source doesn't exist, so have the data produced instead".

㊢ (the six turns, as 象 read them)
| # | Turn | 象's intents | Patterns |
|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | "now I have an idea … transcripts … R-numbers" | explain, propose | 2 read, both rejected |
| C1 | only 4 nodes speak; a corpus plan; 🈸 | (my marks: ㊥ ㊢ 🈖 ㊟ 🈸) | — |
| J2 | "No, let's try a different approach … codex-10 … stepper" | redirect, report | 3 read, all rejected (`name-what-you-drop`, `step-machine`, `scope-bounded-handoff`) |
| C2 | accept; three steps for the narration | (㊥ 🈖 ㊟) | — |
| J3 | "places where there *isn't* good alignment … line 2979" | prioritize, report | `plos-npt-with-small-n/disconfirmation-not-just-triangulation` accepted |
| C3 | six misaligned nodes, R10 the clearest; propose machine-side cues | (㊥ ㊢ 🈖 ㊟ ㊭) | — |

🈖 (operator intent and agent follow-up)
- **J1 to C1.** Your exploratory proposal got a check against the record before any work started. C1 turned it into a priced plan and asked.
- **C1 to J2.** 象's rationale for J2 says the "No" answers C1's finding. So your redirect followed from what my reply had established, not just from a change of mind.
- **J3 to C3.** J3 named what counts as a result, the disagreements. C3 delivered exactly that, and it later went into the MAP section of M-aif-over-the-operator.

In the language of the causal probe: J2 kept the aim fixed and swapped the input. That's an intervention on one variable, which is the kind of thing the joined model can represent.

㊟ (whether the patterns predicted anything)
- **Who mined them.** The three live readings are 象-sonnet's, not Kimi's. Kimi-12 and kimi-13 wrote about 560 of the 5,908 analyses behind the mined pattern graph.
- **The graph's link to J3 isn't a prediction.** The graph does have a next-in-session edge from `cascade-construction/run-it-on-a-real-case` to `disconfirmation-not-just-triangulation`. That first pattern was cited on the turn just before J1, your "whether the keywords actually detect anything". But the edge was built from these turns themselves, and J1 and J2 are skipped because they cite nothing. A fair test would rebuild the graph with these turns held out, and I haven't done that.
- **My replies have no pattern readings.** 象 reads operator turns only. On my own reading, C3 carries out the disconfirmation pattern, but that is my judgement, not a record.

㊭ (making it the exemplar) Two steps, then the join:
1. **Held-out prediction.** Rebuild the mined graph without J1–J3. Then check whether the neighbours of the patterns cited just before J1 rank `disconfirmation-not-just-triangulation`, or the J2 candidates, above chance.
2. **Readings of my replies.** Have 象 read C1–C3 under the same schema, so agent turns get intents and pattern references too.
3. **The join.** Then join the six turns as small open models, sharing names like "transcripts", "narrative at line 2979" and "six-node table". Ask what C3 depends on, and run the knock-out "had J2 not redirected".

🈸 (one decision) Shall I start with step 1, the held-out prediction? It's read-only and quick.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (`C-c ;`) Thanks, found it. `C-c ;` runs `xiaoxiang-insert-mark`, which puts one of 象's intent marks into your turn, and `🈸:yes` answers an agent paragraph. Those marks are already in the 象 analyses: about 25 of your turns carry them, each analysed twice. The most common are 🈸, ㊬ and 🈰. So we can build examples now without waiting for the War Machine, using your marked turns as inputs and my marked replies and commits as outputs.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what's on record) 50 analyses in `~/.emacs-graph/session-turn-analysis/` have a mark in `source_text`. Recent ones include "🈯 What is this? >>>…", "🈰 Please continue with that then" and "㊢ (progress) …". None of them has R-node cues yet. Cue proposals started only after these turns were analysed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how an example would be built) Use the same construction as the cascade probe, with one small open model per exchange:
- **Input:** your marked act, for example 🈰 continue, 🈯 clarify, 🈸 ask, or 🈸:yes on an offer.
- **Owned:** my reply's marked paragraphs and the acts behind them: a commit, a file, a test run.
- **Shared names to join on:** whatever two exchanges both refer to, such as a commit sha, a file path or an offer id.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what it would show of the 象 model)
- **Derivation:** which of your turns a given commit depends on.
- **Knock-outs:** for example, "had you not said 🈰, which deliverables would be missing?"
- **Checkable predictions:** the proforma's "mark honestly" rule becomes something the joined model predicts and the record can falsify. For instance, a ㊬ paragraph should depend on a verification act that exists in that turn's record. If the predictions fail, that tells us either my marks or the model are wrong.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (limits) Exchanges would be joined by the names they share, read off the text and the commit trailers. That reading is mine, so this is a hand-built exemplar like the peripheral one, not something mined automatically.
